entities.summary: Count Andrzej Hieronim Franciszek Zamoyski was a Polish noble (szlachcic) and a prominent figure in the early 18th-century Polish aristocracy. Born into a wealthy family, Zamoyski was educated in the classics and became a skilled diplomat and military leader. He played a key role in the Polish-Russian War of 1768-1774, which aimed to protect Polish sovereignty against Russian expansion. Zamoyski was knighted by King August III in 1758 and received the Order of the White Eagle, the highest honor in Poland. He died on February 10, 1792, at the age of 60. Zamoyski's legacy as a statesman and military leader has endured, with many historians regarding him as one of the most important Polish nobles of his time. His contributions to Polish diplomacy and military strategy continue to be studied by scholars today.
